summary:
The rework answers most of what was accepted last time:
- **M1:** rig runs are now serialized by a named mutex (RigLock), leftovers are swept under it, N-003 and N-004 were added, and "or on kill" is gone.
- **m2:** the rule now catches `_scanTask.WaitAsync`, `Task.WhenAny` and the `Task.Run(...).WaitAsync` chain, and still passes `running.WaitAsync`.
- **m3:** an unset FSA_HOOK_CANCEL_DELAY_MS now means no Cancel.
- **m4:** the hook writes a `returned` stamp and a final line from ShutdownStarted.
- **m6:** N-001 asserts a maximum 1 s gap, and the design says the default run proves only that the line does not appear.
- **m7:** the design says the close escape rests on the loopback rig.
- **O-008:** handled through the engine's own disposition.

The overridden M2 and m5 are not re-opened here.

What the rework introduced or walked past:
- **RigLock is thread-bound.** A .NET Mutex can only be released by the thread that acquired it. The design holds it "for the rig's life", including inside StalledShareTests, which waits about 60 s for a stalled scan under async xUnit. That test has never run since the extraction, so the release-on-another-thread failure would first appear in the person's only run.
- **The staleness path list leaves out code the pass depends on.** It omits the scanner (src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/**), which StalledShareTests and N-001 measure, and App.xaml.cs, whose report-then-Shutdown order N-001's final line depends on. It also relies on a reviewer judging "executable lines" and "the N cases region". Meanwhile the design reuses the pass across a rebase onto uat and plans a separate slice that edits SynchronousIoCancel.
- **Smaller gaps:** rule 4 dropped the eng/**/*.ps1 scope the person accepted. Rule 1 dropped the DriveInfo/File guards. StallRig's added wait argument and N-003's "waits or fails" have no stated default or bound. The sweep's filter coverage is only "expected".

Citations checked and accurate:
- rclone PR #9792 says operations on pooled SMB connections ignored the caller's context, so in-flight SMB I/O could not be interrupted.
- smbprotocol #297 is 'disconnect on exit very slow', an exit that waits on the server's reply to a disconnect.
- The CIFS page is now correctly used only as a pointer.

The Samba-list citation was not checked because nothing leans on it.

findings.claim: RigLock is a named Mutex, 'held for the rig's life', and StalledShareTests shares it through SmbRig.cs. A Mutex belongs to the thread that acquired it: ReleaseMutex from any other thread throws ApplicationException ('Object synchronization method was called from an unsynchronized block of code'). StalledShareTests keeps the rig alive across a scan it waits on for about 60 s. Under async xUnit, the continuation after that wait, and the fixture's Dispose, usually run on a different thread-pool thread from the one that acquired the lock. So release either throws and fails the test at teardown, or is swallowed and leaves the lock held by a pool thread until the test host exits. StallRig has the same problem if its Main awaits stdin asynchronously. Every caller has to remember to acquire and release on one thread. The test has never run since the extraction (+2 -311), so the person's single sitting is the first place this can surface, and it would cost a person-run lap.
findings.evidence: Stall rig component: 'RigLock is a named mutex, Local\\FsAnalyser-SmbRig, held for the rig's life... Linked by StalledShareTests.cs and StallRig'. Case 'run the stalled-share baseline on the extracted rig': 'It compiles but has never run since the extraction'. The thread-affinity failure is documented at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/23153155/named-mutex-with-await ('If the method guarded by a Mutex is synchronous then above code will work but with async I will get: Object synchronization method was called from an unsynchronized block of code').
findings.fix: Make thread affinity impossible to get wrong. RigLock starts its own dedicated thread, which calls WaitOne (treating AbandonedMutexException as acquired) and then blocks on an event until Dispose signals it, then calls ReleaseMutex on that same thread. Callers on any thread only construct and dispose RigLock. This keeps the abandoned-mutex signal for a waiting second run, which a named Semaphore would lose. To check before the person's sitting: search SmbRig.cs for WaitOne and ReleaseMutex, and check whether any holder in StalledShareTests or StallRig keeps the lock across an await. Or add one default-run SmbRigTests case that acquires the lock, awaits Task.Yield() on the thread pool, and disposes.

findings.claim: The rule for when the person's pass goes stale omits code whose behaviour that pass measured. (1) src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/** is missing. StalledShareTests is a test of Scanner on the stalled rig, and N-001 records the measured Cancel-to-return through Scanner and SynchronousIoCancel. Yet the design plans a separate slice for the SynchronousIoCancel flake, which will edit exactly that code, and reuses the pass when rebasing onto uat. (2) src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs is missing. N-001's final line from ShutdownStarted and its exit behaviour depend on the report-write-then-Shutdown order at App.xaml.cs:102-110, which m4 was about. (3) tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj is missing. It fixes the SMBLibrary versions, the linked-source items and the test filter. On top of that, two parts of the rule depend on a reviewer's judgement: 'executable lines' versus comment-only, and 'the N cases and checks of WindowCases.ps1', a region within a file that also holds Update-StallRig and the report readers the N cases use. So the pass can be reused on code it never ran against, with nothing failing.
findings.evidence: Contract 'The person-run network check': 'The pass goes stale only if a later commit changes executable lines in the app files MainWindow.xaml, MainWindow.xaml.cs or StoppingWait.cs, in tests/window/FsaWindowHook/ or tests/window/StallRig/, in SmbRig.cs or StalledShareTests.cs, or in the N cases and checks of WindowCases.ps1.' Key decisions: 'The person's pass is reused unless a listed path changed in executable lines' (trunk conflict), and 'The SynchronousIoCancelTests flake ... is its own slice'. Decision on m4: 'EndingShown triggers WindowReport.WriteAsync and then Shutdown (App.xaml.cs:102-110)'.
findings.fix: Add src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/**, src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs, tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj and eng/read-window.ps1 to the list. Make the pass go stale on any change to a listed path, and treat the whole of WindowCases.ps1 as listed. Replace the general comment-only exemption with one named exemption for the single SmbRig.cs comment commit this slice makes, recorded by its SHA, so no later stage has to judge what is 'executable'.

findings.claim: The person accepted m1 as 'Widen the files to tests/**/*.cs, tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1'. Rule 4 covers only tests/**/*.ps1, so eng/**/*.ps1 was silently dropped. eng/ is where this repo keeps its PowerShell helpers (dotnet.ps1, read-window.ps1, rules-parity.ps1), and an eng-level cleanup helper is a plausible home for a Remove-SmbMapping that bypasses RigLock and the sweep filter.
findings.evidence: Decision m1 (accepted-pending): 'Widen the files to tests/**/*.cs, tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1'. Architecture rule 4 has files 'tests/**/*.ps1'.
findings.fix: Give rule 4 the files tests/**/*.ps1 and eng/**/*.ps1, and grep eng/ for the patterns before declaring it, as the design already does for tests/.

findings.claim: The rework rewrote rule 1 around testability (no clock, no window) and dropped the earlier guards: System.IO* imports, \bDriveInfo\b and (Directory|File) calls. Those guards kept spike 3's invariant, that the UI-thread tick never touches a possibly stalled drive, true for the one function the tick calls. StoppingWait.For is the natural place for a later 'is it a network drive?' wording tweak, which the contract currently forbids ('does not claim the drive is a network drive'). Nothing would now stop one, and such a call made on the UI tick could hang the very line that explains the hang. The only remaining check is N-001's gap assertion, which runs only when a person runs it.
findings.evidence: Rule 1: must_not_import ['System.Windows*', 'Microsoft.Win32*'], must_not_match only matches clock reads and DispatcherTimer. The previous design's rule 1 had must_not_import 'System.IO*' and must_not_match '\bDriveInfo\b', '\b(?:Directory|File)\.\w+\('.
findings.fix: Add back 'System.IO*' to must_not_import, and '\bDriveInfo\b' and '\b(?:Directory|File|Path)\.\w+\(' to must_not_match. Extend the rule's 'because' with the spike 3 reason.

findings.claim: The StallRig launch contract mentions 'an optional wait argument the builder added' without giving its name, its default or any time bound. N-003 accepts either outcome ('waits or fails with a message naming the lock'). If the default is to wait with no bound, a second run behind a hung first run (a live holder that never releases) waits forever. The case would then hang instead of failing, and a person-run sitting would stall with no message.
findings.evidence: Contract 'StallRig launch': 'It has an optional wait argument the builder added.' Error case: 'Lock held by a live run: it waits or fails with a message naming the lock (N-003).' Window cases: 'N-003: a second rig run waits or fails with an error that says why.'
findings.fix: Name the argument in the contract, state its default and a maximum wait (for example, fail after the argument's seconds with the lock name and the holder's PID if known). Have N-003 assert the default behaviour, not either outcome.

findings.claim: The sweep is the only code in the slice that deletes things on the person's machine, yet its filter coverage is stated as an expectation, not a criterion: 'SmbRigTests are expected to cover the filter boundary.' A design that owns the criterion should require it. The shapes are: a different server (including the person's Z: on 100.109.48.75), 7 and 9 hex digits, uppercase, a non-fsa name, and localhost or the IPv6 loopback literal (--1.ipv6-literal.net) that spike 1 used. The tests must also run on the same predicate the sweep calls, not a copy of the regex.
findings.evidence: Case 'sweep leftover rig mappings': 'SmbRigTests are expected to cover the filter boundary.' Stall rig component: 'While holding it the rig sweeps leftover mappings that exactly match the 127.0.0.1 share named fsa plus 8 hex digits.'
findings.fix: Make it a criterion. The sweep's match is one pure predicate in SmbRig.cs, called by the sweep, with default-run SmbRigTests over the listed shapes. Each non-rig shape must be kept, and only \\127.0.0.1\fsa<8 lowercase hex> removed.

dimensions_checked.result: none new. The ~60 s figure is now correctly attributed to this machine's SessionTimeout of 60 and to the rig, not to the CIFS page. Cited prior art was checked. rclone PR #9792 (https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/9792) says pooled SMB connections used the caller's context only while dialling, so cancelling could not interrupt in-flight I/O; that matches the design's claim. smbprotocol #297 (https://github.com/jborean93/smbprotocol/issues/297) is 'disconnect on exit very slow', an exit that waits on the disconnect response; that matches, and the design correctly hedges it as not a kernel-level analogue. The recalled claims (Local\\ is scoped to the terminal-services session; elevated and unelevated tokens have separate logon sessions and so separate mapping tables) are consistent with Windows behaviour and are not load-bearing beyond the acknowledged 'fails loudly' path.
The earlier concurrent and killed-run shapes are now cases N-003 and N-004 (my previous M1 is answered). A new gap: N-003 has no bound when a live holder hangs (m3).
M1: the RigLock Mutex belongs to one thread, so every holder must remember to acquire and release on the same thread. The fix is to confine that to one dedicated thread inside RigLock.

none: RigLock, the sweep, four N cases, a self-contained StallRig and 19 synthetic logs are a lot for a UI-text change. Each answers a measured constraint, though: one port per server name, no machine-wide .NET 10 runtime, and only a person may change SMB mappings.

M2: the staleness path list omits Core/Scanning, App.xaml.cs and the Core.Tests csproj, and leans on judging 'executable lines' and regions within a file. m3: the StallRig wait argument and N-003's outcome are unspecified. The earlier m3 (CANCEL_DELAY default) and m4 (collapse observability) are answered.

Killed holder: answered by the sweep under the lock. Other-session leftover: New-SmbMapping fails loudly, which is acknowledged. Marker absent: the hook refuses after 60 s. A lock released on the wrong thread is covered in M1. A hung live holder is covered in m3.

m1: the person's accepted m1 scope (eng/**/*.ps1) was dropped from rule 4. Everything else matches the recorded decisions. M2 and m5 stay overridden, and are respected here and not re-opened. m6's build-time -IncludeNetwork was declined by decision and is not re-filed.

m2: rule 1 lost its drive and IO guards in the rewrite. Rule 2 as rewritten now matches `_scanTask.WaitAsync(`, `Task.WhenAny(` and the `Task.Run(...).WaitAsync(` chain, and not `running.WaitAsync(token)`, so the earlier m2 is answered. Rules 3 and 4 add `net use`, New-SmbGlobalMapping and WNet*, which answers the earlier m1 except for the eng/ scope.

m4: the sweep-filter boundary is only 'expected' to be covered. The design now says openly that C-006 proves only that the line does not appear, and N-001 carries the UI-liveness gap assertion; both answer the earlier m6. The faulted and finished-on-its-own shapes are recorded as not fed by any test, with a reason.

none: the sweep is limited to \\\\127.0.0.1\\fsa<8 hex> in the caller's own logon session, so the person's Z: on 100.109.48.75 is out of reach, provided the predicate is tested as m4 asks. The server is loopback-only, nothing elevates, and the hook's env vars are test-only.
